title: Same Tree
description: Match empty subtrees, reject missing nodes or different values, then recursively compare the corresponding left and right children.
note: Two empty subtrees match. A missing node on only one side means the trees have different shapes, even when their remaining values are equal.
notes: The guard order and recursive calls follow the Python solution. Python uses truthiness for the supplied TreeNode references; Birdie explicitly checks optional absence with == none.
Comparisons with none check presence without invoking record equality. General record equality remains undecided; this algorithm explicitly compares each value and the shape of both trees.

or evaluates from left to right and skips later operands once one is true. p.val != q.val is reached only after both absence checks are false, so p and q are known to be TreeNode values. After the guard is passed, the remaining body retains those presence facts.
and also short-circuits. A left-subtree mismatch returns false without visiting the right subtrees. The result is a bool rather than an operand value.
LeetCode supplies TreeNode. The record declaration shows its standalone Birdie form. The algorithm does not modify either tree, and an empty tree matches another empty tree.
For two matching trees with n nodes and height h, the traversal takes O(n) time and O(h) recursion space in the usual unit-cost model. A mismatch can stop the traversal earlier.
